title: Multi-Stakeholder Platforms Enhancing Sustainable Agriculture
reason: Transcript discusses various sustainable agricultural practices, multi-stakeholder platforms, and the importance of considering externalities in food systems.

tasks.task: Describe the concept of multi-stakeholder platforms and their application in agriculture.

subtasks.text: Explain that multi-stakeholder platforms bring together different stakeholders from the agricultural field to define programs and projects together.
Mention the term "co-producer" and its relevance in involving consumers in the discussion of production methods.

tasks.task: Present the concept of re-internalizing externalities through pricing to make consumers aware of the true costs of food production.

subtasks.text: Provide a real-life example of how production and pollution are externally costed to the public rather than the producers.
Explain the importance of re-internalizing both negative and positive externalities through pricing and subsidies.

tasks.task: Address the challenge small holder farmers face with economies of scale and potential solutions through tailored scientific innovation.

subtasks.text: Highlight the large contribution of small holder farmers to global food production and the need for tailored solutions.
Describe how technology can help small holder farmers reduce resource use by using precision methods.

tasks.task: Discuss the role of FAO in promoting sustainable practices and the tension between reforestation and agricultural needs.

subtasks.text: Describe the challenge of reforestation in Latin America versus Europe.
Provide an example of how coffee can be grown sustainably while still being economically viable for farmers.
